clue.text: See 3
Every man Jack freezes outside a northern 27 …

parts.note: every man Jack is an idiom for everybody, all of them

indicators.note: outside says the frozen-water word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: freezes, as a noun, is ice

explanation.surface: Every last man freezes outside some northern trade union, as if on a winter picket line.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 27 is UNION, the second word of CREDIT UNION. 'outside' puts ICE around A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A union of parties or states joined for a common purpose is a pact or league of that kind.

clue.text: … wheel them around wedding venue's back passage

parts.note: to wheel is to turn round, to spin

indicators.note: around says the word for everyone goes round the biblical village

parts.note: the ellipsis carries on from the clue before, so them points back to every man Jack, that is all
Cana in Galilee is where the wedding took place at which water was turned into wine

explanation.surface: Wheel the wedding guests round to the passage at the back of the venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them' only works as a continuation of the previous clue, pointing back to 'Every man Jack'. 'back passage' sounds coarse but means a passage in the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The channel running down the back through the vertebrae, carrying the cord of nerves, is a passage in the back.

clue.text: Take a chance? Prolific sketcher will!

definitions.meaning: to choose by picking tickets at random, leaving the result to luck
read literally, a prolific artist makes a great many drawings

explanation.surface: Should you gamble? An artist who sketches all day certainly will.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: someone who sketches a lot will produce plenty of pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling something by picking straws or tickets at random is leaving it to chance, a gamble.

clue.text: Glimpse exposed finger wound at printing-house

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters of the wound are removed

parts.note: a cut from the edge of a sheet, the kind of injury expected among stacks of print

explanation.surface: A quick look at a printer's sore finger shows an open cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' strips the first and last letters, P and T, off PAPER CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperçu is a brief insight or quick sight of something, a fleeting view, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Nervelessness fighting under commander having to take risks

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the fighting word below the officer's letters

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer
fighting is war
to dice, as in dicing with death, is to gamble or take risks

explanation.surface: A soldier serving under a reckless officer would need some nerve in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking nerve is lacking courage, so nervelessness is a want of bravery, being a coward.

clue.text: Spanish and Estonian composers go to pieces!

parts.note: Manuel de Falla was a Spanish composer; the plural composers covers both names
Arvo Pärt is an Estonian composer

explanation.surface: Two composers from opposite ends of Europe are going to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composers' applies to both nationalities: Falla is Spanish and Pärt Estonian.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pieces is to break down or collapse, whether a thing or a person under stress.

clue.text: See 21
Like a fool sets about papers?

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for sets is read backwards

parts.note: sets, as in sets down, puts
ID, identity documents, are papers

explanation.surface: Only a fool would set down papers carelessly, or so the question suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A foolish person is dim and senseless, so behaving as a fool would is being dense.

clue.text: 16 into an eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of into an are rearranged

explanation.surface: A race of people turned into an eccentric bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 16 is RACE, the last word of EGG-AND-SPOON RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A people sharing descent and culture, the old sense of a race, is a nation.

clue.text: 1 perhaps caught unpopular person out?

indicators.note: caught, as in heard, says the phrase is taken by ear

parts.note: a wart is slang for an unpopular person, and away means out, not at home

explanation.surface: Caught out, the unpopular person was revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 1 is CANAL, an example of the answer, hence 'perhaps'. Said aloud, WART AWAY gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is an example of a navigable channel for boats, man-made rather than a river.

clue.text: 16 corners

definitions.meaning: the cross-reference is race; the ... were a Germanic people who settled England
corners are places where two lines or walls meet at a slant

explanation.walkthrough: 16 is RACE: the Angles were a people, the source of the name England.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner is where two lines meet; the Angles were a tribe from northern Germany, a people or race.

clue.text: 16 between 10s was to probe this Special One

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: The Cold War rivalry between superpowers was to explore this; and a manager styled himself the Special One.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is RACE and 10 is NATION: the race between nations in the 1960s was to explore the cosmos.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmos beyond Earth's atmosphere was what the superpowers' Cold War race set out to explore.

clue.text: See 28
In springtime, well-organised individual will miss European 27

indicators.note: In says the following pieces go inside the spring month

parts.note: May is a month of spring
trim means neat, well-organised

indicators.note: will miss says the abbreviation for European is dropped

parts.note: one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A tidy person, in spring, will skip the European wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 27 is UNION, the second word of CREDIT UNION. 'will miss' and 'In' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage is a joining of two people, a union in the formal sense of the word.

clue.text: See 21
Instrument, an organ newly built, keeping diameter constant

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the rebuilt letters hold the next pieces
newly built says the letters of an organ are put together afresh

parts.note: pi is the mathematical constant

explanation.surface: A newly built organ is fitted with pipes of constant diameter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly built' rearranges AN ORGAN into GRANANO, split by 'keeping' to hold D and PI. Pi links a circle's diameter to its circumference.
explanation.definitionFit: The large concert keyboard with horizontal strings is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Rising smoke envelops pasture of northern 16

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means read upwards, so the letters are reversed
envelops says the smoke word wraps round the pasture word

parts.note: cig is slang for a cigarette, a smoke
a lea is a meadow or pasture

explanation.surface: Smoke rising over a field in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is RACE: the Gaels are the Celtic peoples of Scotland and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the Celtic peoples of Scotland, Ireland and the Isle of Man, a northern people.

clue.text: 1 boat ultimately something to chew over

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the chewed word is read backwards

parts.note: cud is what a cow chews

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of boat

explanation.surface: A canal boat gives one something to chew over.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 is CANAL; a duct or tube in the body is a canal.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal in anatomy is a tube or channel carrying fluid, such as the ear's passage.

clue.text: Hamlet perhaps retains opening for scout to employ ballerina

indicators.note: retains means holds inside, so the scout's initial sits within the European

parts.note: Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark, an example of a Dane

indicators.note: opening for picks the first letter of scout

parts.note: to employ is to use

explanation.surface: A Hamlet production hires a ballerina through a talent scout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' looks like the play or a village; it is the prince, a Dane. 'retains' puts S inside DANE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a female dancer is used in English for a ballet dancer.

clue.text: Down which East End scamperer descends to form area for growth?

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End drop their aitches, so the H goes from each word

parts.note: a hare is an animal that scampers
a hole in the ground is what the animal goes down, as the clue's descends spells out

explanation.surface: A Cockney rabbit runs down its burrow to make room to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech, from London's East End, drops the H: 'ARE and 'OLE. The hole is the place 'down which' the hare descends, so it comes after the hare.
explanation.definitionFit: On a cactus, an areole is the small patch from which spines and flowers sprout, a site for growth.

clue.text: Moon, after removing belt, stag night's designated driver?

indicators.note: a belt goes round the outside, so removing it strips the first and last letters

parts.note: the designated driver at a bachelor party is the sober one

explanation.surface: A man moons at the stag night after removing his belt, while the driver looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag night is a British bachelor party. 'after removing belt' takes S and E off SOBER ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is one of the moons of Uranus, named after the fairy king in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Urge to kiss and cuddle a dancer, worried about competition

parts.note: to egg on is to urge

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the cuddling word
worried means agitated, so the letters of a dancer are shuffled

parts.note: to spoon is old slang for courting, kissing and cuddling

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to kiss and cuddle a dancer who is anxious about a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoon' is old-fashioned slang for courting. 'worried' rearranges A DANCER into ANDRACE, which 'about' splits around the courting word.
explanation.definitionFit: A school sports day event in which runners balance an egg on a spoon is a race or contest.

clue.text: Set up namely for one to catch fine lizards

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means raised upwards, so the letters are read in reverse
to catch says the namely abbreviation holds the fine word

parts.note: sc. (scilicet) is the Latin abbreviation for namely
OK means fine
eg means for example, for one

explanation.surface: Namely, a trap was set up to catch fine lizards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' puts OK in SC, giving SOKC; add EG, and 'Set up' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small tropical lizards with sticky toe pads that let them climb walls.

clue.text: See 17 across
Risk about a 17 Across

indicators.note: about here means around, so the risk word goes round the article

parts.note: to imperil is to put at risk

explanation.surface: Taking a chance on something majestic.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 Across here stands for its first word on its own, used as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposing and majestic, befitting an emperor, matches the sense of magnificent or stately.

clue.text: See 4
Reduction in flexible means to save

indicators.note: flexible means able to bend, so the letters of reduction in are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cut in a flexible plan is a way to save money.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooperative savings and lending body owned by its members is a way for people to put money by.

clue.text: See 26
17 Across 23 brought in at home issuing fifth note with fantastic sound

indicators.note: brought in says the musical abbreviation is put inside the rest
issuing means sending out, so a letter leaves the home word

parts.note: a house is a home
E is the fifth of the musical notes A to G
and means with

indicators.note: fantastic means wild, so the letters of sound are rearranged

parts.note: the cross-reference is the keyboard instrument; p is its abbreviation, meaning soft in music

explanation.surface: A concert instrument is brought into a house, giving out a fifth note with a fantastic sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 Across here is its first word alone, British slang for £1,000. 23 is PIANO, abbreviated as in music. 'issuing', 'fantastic' and 'brought in' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the cross-referenced word for a sum of one thousand in sterling.
